data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'Kur', meaning 'man' or 'dedication'. In the Old Testament, the name Curtis is borne by the grandson of Judah and the father of Asher. In Christianity, it is associated with the virtue of courage. The name Curtis carries the meaning “Man, or dedication” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Curtis usually hope their child will grow to embody man, or dedication and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קורטיס מקורו בשם הלטיני קורטיקוס שמשמעותו נימול או קצר. הוא קשור למילה הלטינית 'קורטוס' שפירושה חצר או שטח סגור. השם נמצא בשימוש נרחב בתרבויות נוצריות ומשויך לתכונות של צניעות ושמירת גבולות.

in_greek.name: Κούρτις
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κούρτις προέρχεται από το Λατινικό όνομα Curticus, που σημαίνει κοντός ή κομμένος. Στην αρχαία Εκκλησία, το όνομα συνδέθηκε με την έννοια της κοπής ή της αφαιρέσεως, συμβολίζοντας την πνευματική κοπή από τον κόσμο και την προσάρτηση στο Θεό.

in_latin.name: Curtis
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Curtis originates from the Latin term 'cohors' or 'curtis', meaning a courtyard or an enclosed area. It evolved into 'Curticus', signifying short or cut. In early Christian tradition, the name conveyed humility and courteous demeanor, essential virtues for a devout Christian.

Beyond the historical and biblical roots, the name Curtis has come to symbolize courage and dedication, reflecting the steadfast commitment and fortitude expected of a follower of Christ. data.spiritual_symbolism: Curtis, from the Latin word "curtus," meaning short or brief, symbolizes one who is focused and committed to their chosen path. Spiritually, it represents an individual deeply connected to their inner wisdom, making decisions with clarity and brevity.

historical_references.reference: Curtis, a Roman praenomen or personal name in common use during the Roman Republic, is derived from the Latin verb 'curare', meaning 'to take care of'. The name was often given to a child born after the death of a sibling, as a symbol of taking care of the family and keeping the memory of the deceased alive.

St. Curtis of Tarsus, a Christian martyr, is believed to have been born in Tarsus, Cilicia, around the late 2nd or early 3rd century AD. He is said to have been a soldier in the Roman army who, after converting to Christianity, was martyred for his faith during the persecutions under Emperor Maximian. The exact details of his life and martyrdom are not well documented, but he is venerated as a patron saint of soldiers and is sometimes included in the list of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste.
